title: Emit valid compressed frames for empty messages
goal: Handle the changed output of a finalised Deflate or GZip stream that receives no writes.

selectionNotes: Handle the changed output of a finalised Deflate or GZip stream that receives no writes. Desktop/server examples; inspect complete constraints before use.

runtime.name: .NET
runtime.reason: This edition uses or relies on .NET 11 framework APIs/behaviour; .NET 10 is comparison-only.

sdk.name: .NET SDK
sdk.reason: Build the declared net11.0 comparison with its matching SDK.

language.name: C#
language.reason: The canonical .NET 11 project selects its supported C# 15 default.

platforms: Desktop/server .NET platforms; authoring execution recorded on Windows. Browser/WASI excluded from these samples.
prerequisites: Use a net11.0 console project with LangVersion=15.0, implicit usings and the namespaces stated in the complete recipe. No additional package, workload, account or provider is required.
constraints: The exact two-byte raw Deflate and twenty-byte GZip outputs are measured baselines, not a protocol promise about all settings/future encoders. Deflate, ZLib and GZip use different framing and are not interchangeable; Brotli and Zstandard are separate formats too. This change concerns no writes at all; do not infer every stream operation from that case. Use decompressed content length or an explicit application envelope to distinguish empty payload from missing data. Flush alone does not finish a frame. leaveOpen retains ownership of the underlying stream; disposing the compressor still finalises its frame.
stabilityLimitations: Verified with SDK 11.0.100-rc.2.26504.105; RC2 execution is not GA verification.

evidence.scope: Actual .NET 10 Windows compilation/execution: fresh Deflate/ZLib/GZip stream round trips and no-write empty-output baseline. Built-in Zstandard is explicitly unavailable and its stub is tested. No mocks, cross-compilation or GA proof.

The same original source executes on .NET 10 and RC2: no-write outputs are 0/0 bytes versus 2/20 bytes, and both APIs restore empty content. Nonempty payload round trips are checked separately. Actual Windows compilation/execution; no mocks, cross-compilation or GA proof.

humanProof.scope: Bounded desktop/server archive and codec checks run locally without external providers or UI. No extra native/device or external-tool interoperability claim.
